A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DriverGaze360 study. All 13 pages in each version, including supplementary text, figures, tables, algorithms and equations, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original data collected from human drivers, benchmark results on DriverGaze360 and DADA-2000, and an attended-object supervision ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluated panoramic baselines in supplementary Table 7.

M1.justification: The Video Swin backbone, shared decoder, attention and attended-object heads, training losses, and extraction/calibration algorithms are unchanged. The new panoramic comparison does not modify the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain DriverGaze360 and DADA-2000, with the same driving scenarios and participant coverage. The added panoramic baselines use the existing task rather than introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Section 11 and Table 7 add evaluated PanoConv and PAVER baselines adapted to rectilinear inputs. The five original comparison methods in Tables 4 and 5 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented splits, 16-frame inputs, resolutions, metrics, optimizer and training budget are unchanged. The added comparison uses the existing rectilinear inputs; no separate evaluation protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: The attention-only, object-segmentation and attended-object ablation in Table 6 and the qualitative examples are retained unchanged. Table 7 adds ordinary baseline comparisons, not a new robustness test or ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for model performance. The new table continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds PanoConv scores of 1.450/0.599/0.425/5.540 and PAVER scores of 3.375/0.089/0.070/0.236 in KLD/CC/SIM/NSS order. The proposed method's scores are repeated from Table 4; Tables 4–6 and existing qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The metric definitions, loss equations and supplementary fixation-map formulation are mathematically unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dataset, joint-prediction and attended-object extraction contributions, along with the same performance and generalization claims.

C2.justification: New Section 12 explicitly identifies simulation-induced differences in behavior and gaze, advises caution about real-world generalization, and proposes domain adaptation. Section 11 also qualifies the panoramic comparison by distinguishing rectilinear inputs from equirectangular imagery.

D1.justification: The stated project address changes from av.dfki.de to dfki-av.github.io. v2 clarifies rectilinear camera geometry and credits CVC-provided navigation-route code. Existing training and hardware details remain unchanged; baseline adaptation details are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds discussion and citations for SAGE and ASIAFNet. Supplementary Section 11 adds PanoConv and PAVER and explains their input-representation distinction, modestly broadening positioning against related approaches.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments and supplementary Sections 11–12 and expands the related-work paragraph. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 7 is added, Algorithm 1 moves from page 6 to page 5, and Table 1's caption moves above the table. Paragraph spacing and placement shift, while the existing figures and result-table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The panoramic baseline comparison in Table 7 strengthens empirical context, the added related work improves positioning, and Section 12 appropriately qualifies real-world generalization. These are useful, limited improvements: the original evidence is unchanged, and the new baseline adaptations remain insufficiently documented for a substantial increase in confidence.
